sources.title: nsenter and Linux PID-namespace lifecycle semantics
sources.sections_read: PID namespace description, --target, --pid and forking behavior
sources.confirmed: nsenter can enter a target process's PID namespace; it normally forks so the executed program and children share that namespace and see one another.
sources.limits: Not a pod policy API; namespace lifetime, PID 1 behavior and procfs setup require explicit treatment. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: post_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C06.json.

sources.sections_read: Namespaces schema, path handling, pid example and default filesystem list
sources.confirmed: A pid namespace entry with an absolute path joins an existing namespace; omitting path creates a namespace, while omitting the namespace type inherits the runtime namespace.
sources.limits: Omitting the pid type inherits the runtime namespace; the orchestrator still owns pod policy and namespace lifetime.
